is not a gate: start it directly; it is session-owned without a lease.

  -h, --help          Show this help

USAGE
}

GATE_TIMEOUT="${DEX_GATE_TIMEOUT:-0}"

  case "$1" in

# csv-rfc4180

A CSV parser, streaming parser and serializer for Node.js with no dependencies.
It follows RFC 4180 and also accepts LF and CR line breaks, other delimiters,
and a leading byte order mark.

```js
const { parse, createParser, stringify, CsvError } = require('./src/csv');
```

Requires Node.js 18 or later. Run the tests with `npm test`.

## parse(text, options)

```js
parse('name,qty\r\n"Widget, large",3\r\n');
// [['name', 'qty'], ['Widget, large', '3']]

parse('name,qty\nWidget,3\n', { header: true });
// [{ name: 'Widget', qty: '3' }]

parse('a;b\n\n1;2', { delimiter: ';', skipEmptyLines: true });
// [['a', 'b'], ['1', '2']]
```

Options:

| option           | default | meaning                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `delimiter`      | `','`   | one character, not `"`, CR or LF                             |
| `header`         | `false` | use the first record as column names and return objects      |
| `skipEmptyLines` | `false` | drop lines with no characters instead of returning `['']`   |

Every field is a string, and whitespace is never trimmed. A field starting with
`"` is quoted: delimiters and line breaks inside it are literal, `""` is one
`"`, and the closing quote must be followed by a delimiter, a line break or the
end of input. A `"` anywhere else in an unquoted field is an ordinary character.

## createParser(options)

```js
const parser = createParser({ header: true });
parser.write('id,na');     // []
parser.write('me\n1,Ada'); // []  (the header record is not returned)
parser.write('\n2,Grace'); // [{ id: '1', name: 'Ada' }]
parser.end();              // [{ id: '2', name: 'Grace' }]
```

`write(chunk)` returns the records whose terminating line break is in `chunk`.
`end()` returns whatever is left. The combined output, and any `CsvError`
including its position, is the same as `parse` on the joined input, however
the input is split. After `end()` or after any throw, both methods throw an
`Error` whose `cause` is the original failure, if there was one.

Each code unit is read once. A field that spans chunks is kept as a list of
slices and joined when it ends, so memory and time grow with the input, not
with the number of `write` calls times the input.

## stringify(rows, options)

```js
stringify([['a', 'b c'], ['x,y', 'say "hi"']]);
// 'a,b c\r\n"x,y","say ""hi"""\r\n'

stringify([{ id: 1, name: 'Ada' }, { id: 2 }], { header: ['id', 'name'], eol: '\n' });
// 'id,name\n1,Ada\n2,\n'
```

| option      | default  | meaning                                                   |
| ----------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delimiter` | `','`    | same rules as `parse`                                     |
| `eol`       | `'\r\n'` | `'\r\n'` or `'\n'`; written after every record            |
| `header`    | none     | array of column names; allows object rows                 |

Strings are written as they are, numbers and booleans with `String()`, and
`null` and `undefined` as empty fields. Other types throw `TypeError`. A field
is quoted when it contains the delimiter, `"`, CR or LF, or begins or ends
with a space.

For rows that are non-empty arrays of strings, `parse(stringify(rows, opts),
opts)` returns `rows`, with or without `skipEmptyLines`. Each function ignores
options that only the other one reads, so the same object works for both.

## Errors

Malformed input throws `CsvError`, which extends `Error` and has 1-based
`line` and `column` properties (columns count UTF-16 code units) and a `code`:

| code                   | position reported                                    |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `UNCLOSED_QUOTE`       | the opening `"` of the field that is never closed    |
| `INVALID_AFTER_QUOTE`  | the character after the closing `"`                  |
| `DUPLICATE_HEADER`     | the start of the second field with that name         |
| `FIELD_COUNT_MISMATCH` | column 1 of the line where the bad record starts     |

CRLF counts as one line break, including inside quoted fields. When the input
has several problems, the first one found reading left to right is thrown. A
record's field count is checked when the record ends.

Invalid arguments (a non-string `text` or chunk, a bad delimiter, a non-boolean
`header`, an unsupported value type) throw `TypeError`.

## Decisions and assumptions

The specification left these points open. This is how they were resolved.

- **BOM and columns.** A leading U+FEFF is dropped before anything is counted,
  so the code unit after it is column 1. Only the first code unit of the whole
  input is checked, including when the first `write` chunks are empty.
- **Delimiter width.** "A single character" means one UTF-16 code unit
  (`delimiter.length === 1`). A character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane,
  such as an emoji, is rejected with `TypeError`.
- **What `skipEmptyLines` skips.** Only lines with no characters at all. A line
  holding `""` is a record with one empty field and is kept, which is what lets
  `stringify` preserve `['']` through a round trip.
- **Empty lines in header mode.** Without `skipEmptyLines`, an empty line is
  the record `['']`, so it is a field-count error unless the header has exactly
  one column. An empty first line becomes a header with one column named `''`.
- **When duplicates are detected.** A duplicate header name is reported when
  the repeated field ends, because that is the point where a single
  left-to-right read can know the name. So `a,a,"x` reports the duplicate, not
  the unclosed quote.
- **Record objects.** Rows are plain objects with one own property per column,
  in header order. A column named `__proto__` is stored as an ordinary property
  rather than changing the prototype. JavaScript lists integer-like keys such
  as `"1"` before other keys no matter where they appear in the header.
- **Streaming and CRLF.** A record ending in CRLF is returned by the `write`
  that contains the CR. If the next chunk starts with LF, that LF is treated
  as the second half of the same line break.
- **Option validation.** `options` must be an object. `header` and
  `skipEmptyLines` for parsing must be booleans when given. For `stringify`,
  `header` must be an array of strings (or omitted/`false`). Unknown keys are
  ignored.
- **Header with no rows.** `stringify([], { header: ['a', 'b'] })` writes the
  header line, `'a,b\r\n'`. "No rows gives `''`" applies when there is no
  header either.
- **Object rows.** Only own properties are read, so a column named `toString`
  is empty for `{}` instead of picking up `Object.prototype.toString`. Array
  rows are still accepted when `header` is set and are written unchanged.
- **Lone empty field.** A record whose only field is empty (`['']`, `[null]` or
  `[undefined]`) is written as `""`. A record with no fields (`[]`) is written
  as an empty line.
- **Leading U+FEFF in output.** If the first line of the output would start
  with U+FEFF (a first field beginning with it, or an empty first field when
  U+FEFF is the delimiter), that field is quoted. Otherwise the parser would
  take it for a byte order mark and the round trip would lose it.
- **Duplicate names in `stringify`'s header** are not rejected. The output is
  valid CSV, but `parse` with `header: true` will refuse it.

## Layout

| file                | contents                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/csv.js`        | public entry point                                |
| `src/parser.js`     | state machine behind `parse` and `createParser`   |
| `src/stringify.js`  | serializer                                        |
| `src/options.js`    | option validation shared by both directions       |
| `src/errors.js`     | `CsvError`                                        |

content.text:
I've built the CSV library: `src/csv.js` (CommonJS) exports `parse`, `createParser`, `stringify` and `CsvError`, with no dependencies. The full test suite (196 tests) passes through the Dex gate, and a syntax check of all files is clean.

**Layout.** `src/csv.js` is the entry point. The real code is in `src/parser.js`, `src/stringify.js`, `src/options.js` and `src/errors.js`. `parse` just feeds the whole string to the streaming parser in one piece, so chunked input can't give a different result or error position than whole input. Each character is read once, and a field that spans chunks is joined only when it ends, so time and memory grow with the input size.

**Tests.** There are five files under `test/`, one each for `parse`, `stringify`, error positions, streaming and round trips. `npm test` runs them (`node --test`).
- **Chunk splits:** 22 inputs, valid and invalid, are fed through every 2-way and 3-way split plus one character at a time, and each result must match `parse` exactly.
- **Round trips:** random tables are checked under 7 delimiters, both line endings, and with and without `skipEmptyLines`.
- **Speed:** a stress test feeds over 300,000 one-character chunks; it takes about 28 ms.
- **Do the tests catch bugs?** I broke the code on purpose in eight places (for example, splitting a CRLF across chunks, or dropping the end of a field at a chunk boundary). The suite caught every one.

**Fixed during testing:**
- **Wrong error position:** a duplicate header name that ends at end of input (header `,` or `k,,`) was reported at the first field's position. It's fixed, with a regression test.
- **Invisible characters:** the file-writing tool had saved my `\uFEFF` and similar escapes in the tests as literal invisible characters. I changed them back to escapes.

**Choices where the spec was open**, all listed in the README:
- **BOM:** a leading byte order mark doesn't count as a column, so the character after it is column 1.
- **Delimiter:** "one character" means `delimiter.length === 1`, so an emoji delimiter is rejected with `TypeError`.
